messages.text: Littler powers past Aspinall to reach European Championship quarter-finals

metadata.summary: Luke Littler remains on course to win the one major title he's never won as he beat Nathan Aspinall 10-5 in the second round of the European Championship Darts on Saturday evening.
metadata.content: Luke Littler still on course to win European Championship Darts after second-round win over Nathan Aspinall | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Luke Littler still on course to win European Championship Darts after second-round win over Nathan Aspinall The Nuke secures the second highest three-dart average in the history of the tournament as he powers into quarter-finals; Watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22 By Stephen Mills and Raz Mirza Saturday 24 October 2026 22:15, UK Image: Luke Littler celebrates his win over Nathan Aspinall at the European Championship Luke Littler remains on course to win the one major title he's never won as he beat Nathan Aspinall 10-5 in the second round of the European Championship Darts on Saturday evening. Littler produced the second-best average in the competition's history - his 114.47 has only ever been bettered by Phil Taylor's 118.14 - as he secured an impressive victory in Dortmund. Aspinall produced ten 180s in the match - three more than his opponent - but it wasn't enough to survive the onslaught from the world No 1, who won the first four legs of the match in 12 darts or fewer. Aspinall briefly rallied to reduce the score to 5-4, but Littler controlled the second half of the game and, despite one brief interruption to deal with a vocal fan in the crowd, he ultimately closed out the match on D10. messages.text: Alonso 'out-coached', 'petulant' Palmer and Penders howler: Chelsea's horror night

metadata.summary: They say bad things come in threes. That was certainly the case for Chelsea on a miserable evening at Stamford Bridge as they lost 2-0 to Tottenham in a game where they were described as "awful" by Gary Neville.
metadata.content: Chelsea: Cole Palmer red card, Mike Penders howler and 'out-coached' by Roberto De Zerbi on horror night for Xabi Alonso | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Chelsea: Cole Palmer red card, Mike Penders howler and 'out-coached' by Roberto De Zerbi on horror night for Xabi Alonso Tottenham won at Stamford Bridge for just the second time in 36 visits in the Premier League; Chelsea created very little in the defeat with Gary Neville calling them 'awful'; Cole Palmer was described as 'petulant' following his red card; Mike Penders made a 'monumental' error Saturday 24 October 2026 21:42, UK Image: Cole Palmer, Xabi Alonso and Mike Penders were front and centre on a poor night for Chelsea They say bad things come in threes. That was certainly the case for Chelsea on a miserable evening at Stamford Bridge as they lost 2-0 to Tottenham in a game where they were described as "awful" by Gary Neville. Spurs had won only one of their previous 36 league visits to Chelsea but dominated Xabi Alonso's side from start to finish, with an own goal from Mike Penders and a stunning late strike from Mathys Tel securing a well-deserved win for Roberto De Zerbi's side. Saints actually led at half-time at a soaking Mattioli Woods Welford Road, but they had no answer as the Tigers turned on the power to score four tries following the restart.
